title: Tuts Washington gives him a first big job at the Cotton Club
summary: At about 14 he played his first big job with Tuts Washington at the rebuilt Cotton Club on Rampart; also the Tick Tock.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah. That's all they would play in the saloons, was blues. Were they just solo pianists? Yeah. Most of the piano players who were really popular, they played piano and sang too. They would sing and play the piano. And there's a guy who, did you ever hear of Trits Washington? Sure. Yeah. He was the first one to take, he took me on my first big job. So what took you on your first big job? Yeah, at the Cotton Club. Yeah, just built a new place, they had rebuilt a place on Rampart Street where he had gambling and drinking. And it was really a nice place, you know. And he came to my house nice, my mother, because I played there with a lot of people. At that time I was about, I couldn't have been no more than 14. What was the Cotton Club like? It was, well see, there was a Cotton Club there, but you remodel it. Remodel it. When you remodel it, it was, I think they got that name from the Cotton Club in New York. Because I'm more than sure New York had a Cotton Club before in New Orleans. Yeah. Then they had another club, called a Tick Tock. There was a club and they had dancing there too. That was on Rampart Street. Did you work at that club? I never worked there. Although Victor, the band played there, but I had gotten out of the band. I got out of the band before I played at the Tick Tock. Now the senior band would play there a lot. And after I got out of the band, then the senior band started traveling around Louisiana, so they put the junior band in there, the Tick Tock. And the rhythm club,
